chapter: Kid Rena, the Cadillac and Jones's sons
title: Raising musical sons, Sun White and Raymond's degree
summary: Sons in brass bands, Sun White's advice, Raymond's Southern University degree and teaching.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: I see. What did your sons ever play in brass bands much?
Yeah my son and I only played a couple of times. That little one played regular. Minor can give you the history of him. Minor was using him. Yeah I see.
Mmhmm. Well that's so hard for me to remember all the young people.

But my big son he'll alternate. He'll he'll he'll play the bass drum or the snare drum. He sound good. He actually got a better Dixieland beat than a rock and roll. Because of Sun White is responsible for my son. Huh? For my son getting his practical training.
Did they work together or did you work together?

No. When my son was young I formed a band. Oh. You know and I had him playing around all these little places you know. And Sun White used to come around. Mmhmm. Just for me. Cause he didn't know my son. Mmhmm. And give my son ideas on the technique. You know the technique of the drums. But my son come out of a school band. Come out of Coin and Tonlefong and Coins band. Both of them. But the my baby boy he went to Southern University. He studied music up there. When? Uh, from 58 to about 63. Something like that. Huh. He finished college. He got a BA degree. And he's now teaching. Teaching at Xavier Prepper. Yeah. Anytime you see Xavier Prepper band. You hear the man say Raymond Jones. You know you look the one of the tall baby and that's him. Yeah.
